title: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild

nodes.name: Day clock, moon phase, blood moon and rare mount schedule
nodes.purpose: World time job: day length, time-of-day bands, moon phase, the weekly blood-moon timer and the scheduler for a rare mount that appears on a set moon phase

nodes.name: Climate zones, altitude temperature, weather roll and wind
nodes.purpose: World manager pieces that turn a map position into a climate, an altitude-based day and night temperature, a rolled weather type and a wind vector

nodes.name: Player exposure temperature
nodes.purpose: Temperature job that blends day and night climate values, adds a weather offset and chases the result at a limited rate, with hot and cold extreme zones

nodes.name: Cooking pot recipe resolution
nodes.purpose: Turns up to five ingredients into a dish: effect merge, bonus rolls, price, clamping and failure dishes

nodes.name: Hard mode rules
nodes.purpose: Rules for the harder difficulty: enemy tier promotion, enemy health regeneration, damage scaling for boss attackers, weaker healing and shorter enemy notice time

nodes.name: Ecosystem map grid and level sensor
nodes.purpose: Position-to-area lookup over the whole map, plus the kill-count driven scaling that swaps weapons and enemies for stronger ones

nodes.name: Weapon modifiers and pouch limits
nodes.purpose: Weapon bonus flags, random bonus choice and durability bonus, plus the item capacity limits of the inventory

nodes.name: Rigid body, contact impulse and character controller setup
nodes.purpose: Contact impulse filtering, motion type switching by inertia, fixed-with-impulse bodies and the parameter schemas for rigid bodies and character controllers

nodes.name: Chemical system configuration
nodes.purpose: Schema for the material, element and world tables that drive fire, ice, wind and electricity interaction

nodes.name: Per-actor damage parameter schema
nodes.purpose: Schema of the per-actor damage resource: damage source rates, reaction table and status effect settings for fire, ice, electricity, water, lava and curse

nodes.name: Player action and state catalogue
nodes.purpose: Decompiled player action classes and their named tunable parameters: climbing, gliding, knockback, jump attacks and general player behaviour. Only parameter names are decompiled; the values live in resource files that are not in this repository

nodes.name: Horse, motorcycle and water surfing riding
nodes.purpose: Rider-side action classes for horses, the motorcycle, horse swimming and fast water travel, with their named tunable parameters (names only)

nodes.name: Camera modes and interaction targets
nodes.purpose: Camera action class catalogue and the enumerations that classify what the player can target or interact with

cards.name: Day clock units and speed
cards.summary: A full day is 360 time units, 15 units per hour. If the frame delta is 1 at 30 Hz (inferred), the clock advances one in-game minute per real second, so a day lasts 24 real minutes.
cards.behavior: Time of day is a float from 0 to 360, with 15 units per hour and 0.25 units per minute. The default step is one minute of in-game time divided by 30, applied once per update and scaled by the variable-frame-rate delta. If that delta is 1 at the 30 Hz reference rate (inferred, not verified), the clock runs 1 in-game minute per real second and a day lasts 24 real minutes. The clock wraps at 24 hours, adds one to the day counter and runs the new-day logic. The clock does not advance while an event cutscene is active or before the opening demo flag is set, and it is held at 11 hours until a dungeon-finding story flag is set. The new-game start time is 5:15.

constants.name: time units per in-game hour
constants.unit: time units per hour; a day is 360 units

constants.name: step divisor for the default time step
constants.unit: divisor: one in-game minute (0.25 units) divided by 30 gives the step per VFR-scaled update, 30 Hz reference

constants.name: start hour
constants.unit: in-game hour of a new game

constants.name: start minute
constants.unit: in-game minute of a new game

constants.name: story hold hour
constants.unit: in-game hour; time is clamped here until the dungeon-finding flag is set

cards.name: Time-of-day bands
cards.summary: The day is cut into eight named bands from the hour. Each band sets a flag that other systems read, so lighting, NPC schedules and music can switch on a band change.
cards.behavior: Every update the current hour is matched to one of eight bands. Early morning runs from 4 to 7 hours and is split again at 5 hours. Late morning runs 7 to 10, early noon 10 to 13, late noon 13 to 17, early evening 17 to 19, late evening 19 to 21, early night 21 to 24 and late night is everything else, from 0 to 4. When the band changes, the matching game flag is set and the others are cleared. Design lesson: use a few coarse bands with explicit flags instead of polling the raw hour in many systems.

cards.name: Weekly blood moon timer
cards.summary: A timer that accumulates in-game time and flags a special night once it passes seven days. If the night cannot play out, the timer is set to eight days so the event retries at the next new day.
cards.behavior: The blood moon timer grows by the same step as the day clock. At each new day, if the player has left the starting plateau and the timer is above seven days, the timer resets and a blood-day flag is set. The game reports a blood moon tonight from hour 4 on a flagged day. When a new day starts after a blood moon night, the cutscene plays and the timer resets to zero, except in prohibited situations (certain boss areas or relic battles), where the timer is set to eight days so the event comes round again at the next new day. When a new day does not trigger the event, a reserve counter of 150 updates is armed and, when it counts down to zero, the blood-day flag is cleared. Force modes can start the event at 21:30 or just after 23:29. Design lesson: a simple accumulating timer plus a flag gives a recurring event that scripted areas can retry.

constants.name: trigger timer threshold
constants.unit: in-game days of accumulated clock time (7 x 24 h x 15 units = 2520 units)

constants.name: retry value
constants.unit: in-game days; timer is set here when the event is prohibited, so it fires again at the next new day

constants.name: night check hour
constants.unit: in-game hour; a flagged day reports a blood moon tonight from this hour

constants.name: forced night hour
constants.unit: in-game hour of the forced mode at 21:30

constants.name: forced late night offset
constants.unit: time units added after 23:29 by the late forced mode

cards.name: Eight-phase moon cycle
cards.summary: The moon phase is the day count plus one, plus one more after noon, modulo eight. A blood-moon night always shows the full moon.
cards.behavior: The phase index is the number of elapsed days, plus one if the time is past noon, plus one, taken modulo eight. A manual override can replace it. If a blood moon will happen tonight, or it is still the morning after a blood day, the phase is forced to full moon. The phase also gates a rare mount scheduler: when the phase is waxing crescent and the mount is not yet present, the scheduler picks a random appearance hour, makes the mount appear at that hour, and removes it after about two days or when the hour comes round again. The scheduler uses a seven-day week counter and is skipped inside one mountain area.

constants.name: noon split
constants.unit: in-game hour after which the phase index advances

constants.name: random appearance hour bound
constants.unit: exclusive upper bound of the random hour roll, in-game hours

constants.name: mount stay limit
constants.unit: in-game days before the mount is removed

cards.name: Day and night blend factor
cards.summary: A 0 to 1 factor that selects between the day and night temperature tables: 1 at night, ramping to 0 between 4 and 9 hours, flat 0 until 16 hours, ramping back to 1 by 21 hours.
cards.behavior: The multiplier is 1 for the hours outside the day window. From 4 to 9 hours it falls in a straight line from 1 to 0. From 9 to 16 hours it stays at 0. From 16 to 21 hours it rises in a straight line back to 1. The temperature job uses this as the blend weight between the day and night values for the player position, so the air cools gradually over five in-game hours at dusk and warms over five hours at dawn.

cards.name: Altitude temperature curve
cards.summary: Each climate zone stores eleven day and eleven night temperatures at 100-unit height steps from 0 to 1000. The game linearly interpolates between the two samples that bracket the player height.
cards.behavior: Height is clamped at zero or above. The code finds the highest 100-unit band floor at or below the height. Inside a band it blends linearly between the sample at that floor and the sample above it. At or above the top band it uses the top sample unchanged. Outside the main open world the fallback temperature is a fixed mild value. A direct override value (from heat or cold zones) replaces the curve value, and an extra additive override can then be applied. Before the climate resource loads, the constructor fills the day samples from minus 60 at height 1000 to 25 at height 0; the real tuned tables come from a climate resource that is not in this repository.

constants.name: samples per curve
constants.unit: samples per day or night table

cards.name: Heat and cold zone overrides
cards.summary: Zones can push a direct day or night temperature for four updates at a time. Overlapping zones keep the more extreme value, and a huge sentinel means unset.
cards.behavior: A zone calls the day or night setter with a temperature and a hold timer of four is set. The countdown code is not in the files read, so the claim that a zone must call again every update is inferred. When a value is already held, a positive request is kept only if it is hotter than the held one, and a request at or below zero is kept only if it is colder, so the strongest hot or cold zone wins. A held value of 99999 or more means no override. A separate extra offset can be added on top. Any held value makes the temperature job skip the weather offset.

constants.name: unset sentinel
constants.unit: temperature units; at or above this the override is ignored

cards.name: Weather roll by climate
cards.summary: Weather is chosen by a cumulative probability roll over clear, cloudy, rain and heavy rain rates for the current climate. Before a story flag is set, anything except clear or cloudy becomes clear.
cards.behavior: A random number below 99 is compared with the clear rate minus one, then with each later rate in turn, subtracting as it goes. The order is clear, cloudy, rain, heavy rain, and any remainder becomes thunder rain. When a water relic rain effect is on in that climate, the result is clear. After the roll, a story progress flag decides whether bad weather is allowed. Until the flag is set, any result other than clear or cloudy is replaced by clear. Requests to set weather directly set a hold timer of four, and when the second flag is set, a request with a lower type value cannot replace a held higher one. The constructor defaults for the four rates are 60, 20, 15 and 5; they are used before the climate resource loads, and the real per-climate rates are in a resource that is not in this repository.

constants.name: random roll bound
constants.unit: exclusive upper bound of the roll

cards.name: Wind speed and direction
cards.summary: Wind speed is the climate wind power times a per-climate multiplier, then overridden by an expansion-field speed, a map-edge speed or a manual speed that lasts ten updates. Direction is a sine and cosine of a per-climate angle.
cards.behavior: The baseline is zero outside the main field. In the main field it is the current climate wind power multiplied by a per-climate multiplier that can be rerolled. Then three overrides are applied in order: a fixed speed for the expansion field, a fixed speed near the map edge, and a manual speed. Later overrides win. Scripts request the manual wind and a hold timer of ten is set. Direction is the unit vector whose horizontal components come from the sine and cosine of the climate angle in radians; vertical is zero. The constructor default wind power is 5, used before the climate resource loads.

cards.name: Player temperature chase and weather offset
cards.summary: The player temperature moves toward the climate target by at most 0.4 per update, jumps at 100 per update after a teleport, and weather subtracts 1.5 or 3 from the target.
cards.behavior: Each update the target is the day and night values for the player height, blended by the day blend factor, plus a weather offset blended between the current and the next weather by a transition rate. Offsets are 0 for clear, minus 1.5 for cloudy and thunder storm, and minus 3 for rain, heavy rain, snow, heavy snow and any other type. The reported temperature chases the target in a straight line at 0.4 per VFR-scaled update, where 1 delta equals one 30 Hz frame (inferred, unverified). When the player or camera jumps 20 units in one update, or the temperature was set directly, a short boost of 10 updates raises the step to 100 so the value snaps to the new area. A call for an instant change arms the boost for 8 updates. The start value is 23.

constants.name: snap chase step
constants.unit: temperature units per VFR-scaled update while the boost is active

constants.name: teleport detection distance
constants.unit: world units moved in one update

cards.name: Hot and cold extreme zones
cards.summary: In a hot or cold extreme zone the temperature is pushed toward 49.9 or minus 9.9, using an offset capped at 50 or minus 50, and never past the target.
cards.behavior: When the world marks a hot extreme, the job adds an offset that lifts the chased temperature toward 49.9. The offset is the full limit of 50 if the sum stays under the target, otherwise only the gap to the target, and zero if the base is already past it. A cold extreme works the same toward minus 9.9 with a limit of minus 50. The offset is added to the chased value, so ordinary chase smoothing still applies underneath. The two targets are not mirror images of each other, and the source does not say why.

cards.name: Cooking effect merge and duration
cards.summary: Up to five ingredients are summed per effect type. One effect type is kept, two different types cancel, and the duration is 30 seconds per ingredient plus a per-effect base time.
cards.behavior: The pot reads at most five ingredient entries. Plain ingredients add healing and effect level per count. Monster parts add extra duration, extra heart level and extra stamina level, multiplied by count. The effect slots are scanned in order. The first slot with a positive count becomes the dish effect and its strength is the summed level times a per-effect multiplier. If a second different effect type is found, the whole effect is erased and the dish has no effect. The duration is the monster time bonus, plus 30 seconds for each item counted, plus the effect base time times its count. Heart effects add the monster heart bonus and stamina effects add the monster stamina bonus. A medicine recipe that ends with no effect becomes the failure dish. Healing is stored as quarter hearts.

constants.name: seconds per ingredient item
constants.unit: seconds of effect time added per counted item

cards.name: Cooking bonus roll
cards.summary: A bonus roll of 0 to 99 is compared with the best spice success rate plus a per-ingredient-count bonus. Success adds extra healing, strength level or time.
cards.behavior: If bonuses are not forced on, the pot takes the highest success rate among the ingredients and adds a bonus that depends on how many ingredients are in the pot. A number from 0 to 99 must be below the total to succeed. A forced-bonus request skips the roll and an explicit no-random request skips the bonus entirely. On success, a bonus type is chosen. With no effect the bonus is extra healing. For heart-up dishes the bonus is extra level. For stamina dishes the bonus is level or healing, chosen by a coin flip, with a fallback when a side is already at its maximum. For other effects the choice is among healing, level and time, restricted if a side is full. Time bonus adds a fixed bonus time. The per-count success table has constructor defaults of zero at one ingredient and five more for each extra slot, and a loaded config replaces them, clamped between minus 100 and 100. The default bonus time is 300 seconds and a config key replaces it.

constants.name: roll bound
constants.unit: exclusive upper bound of the percent roll

constants.name: success rate config clamp
constants.unit: percent; configured rates are clamped to minus 100 to 100

cards.name: Chaos ingredient roll
cards.summary: A special ingredient replaces the normal bonus with a random jump: extra or maximum healing, extra or minimum level, and a random duration of 1, 10 or 30 minutes.
cards.behavior: When the special extract is in the pot, the normal bonus roll is skipped. A random case of up to four is chosen. The lower cases give extra healing or set healing to the minimum. The upper cases add extra strength level or set the level to its minimum. The lowest two cases are removed when healing is zero or the effect is the heart-up type, and the upper two are removed when there is no effect. Then, if the dish has any duration, a three-way roll sets it to 60, 600 or 1800 seconds. The result can be better or worse than a normal dish, so it is a gamble mechanic.

cards.name: Cooking clamps, hearts, stamina and price
cards.summary: Final dish values are clamped: duration at most 1800 seconds, heart-up in whole hearts of 4 quarter units with a minimum of one heart, stamina in wedges of 200, price rounded up to ten with a floor of 2.
cards.behavior: After all bonuses, healing is truncated to a whole number and clamped to the configured maximum. Dishes with no effect and zero healing heal 1 life unit, a quarter heart as inferred from the heart rounding. A fractional strength between 0 and 1 becomes 1, then it is clamped to the effect maximum. Stamina recover strength is multiplied by 200 to become the stamina amount. Heart-up strength is rounded up to a multiple of 4 quarter hearts and not allowed below 4, and its healing is set to the same value so the new hearts are full. Duration is clamped from 0 to 1800 seconds. For price, each ingredient adds its sell value times count, low-price ingredients count as 1, a per-count multiplier from the config applies, the total is rounded up to the next 10, then limited to the total buy value and raised to at least 2. A special tonic is always priced at 2. The failure dish heals 4 life units by constructor default and a rock-hard dish heals 1; a config key can replace both.

constants.name: stamina amount per strength level
constants.unit: stamina units per level for the stamina recover effect

constants.name: ingredient count multiplier cap
constants.unit: ratio cap when the config table is read

cards.name: Hard mode multipliers
cards.summary: Hard mode halves healing and enemy notice time, multiplies damage from boss-class attackers by 1.5 with a floor of 2, and makes eligible enemies regenerate health.
cards.behavior: The manager holds three multipliers that are all set to 0.5 in the constructor and never changed in this source. One halves any healing amount with a floor of 1. One halves the time an enemy needs to notice the player. Damage from boss-class sources (the two boss profiles, the final beast, one named assassin leader and a list of their projectiles) is scaled by 1.5 and truncated to a whole number, and a result of exactly 1 is raised to 2. Enemy health regeneration applies only to enemy actors with more than 1 life and excludes wolves, bears, the final beast and swarm groups. The check follows the parent actor chain so projectiles inherit from their owner. Strength trial shrines are excluded from enemy promotion.

constants.name: healing and notice multiplier
constants.unit: ratio applied to healing and enemy notice time

constants.name: boss damage multiplier
constants.unit: ratio on integer damage, result truncated

constants.name: minimum scaled damage
constants.unit: life points; a scaled result of exactly 1 becomes this

cards.name: Enemy tier promotion ladder
cards.summary: In hard mode each enemy type is swapped for the next stronger variant of the same family, up to a top tier, unless it has a unique name or a no-promotion flag.
cards.behavior: On placement, an enemy whose name starts with the enemy prefix is looked up in a fixed chain. Common ladders run weak, middle, strong, dark and gold variants. Some families stop at strong, and some have only two steps. Unique-named placements and placements flagged to never rank up are skipped, and so are strength trial shrines. The function returns the next name or nothing. A note in the source says two entries are duplicated by mistake; the duplicates have no effect. Design lesson: a name-to-next-name table is the cheapest way to implement tiered enemies.

cards.name: Kill-count difficulty scaling
cards.summary: Points are the sum of a per-enemy value times the defeat count. Weapon and enemy points are that sum times two power factors. Placed weapons and enemies upgrade along ladders when the points pass a rung.
cards.behavior: Each tracked enemy type has a point value and a defeat counter in game data. Unique enemies count once. The total is the sum of value times count, unless a default point value of zero or more is set, which replaces it. Two settings multiply the total to give separate weapon points and enemy points. When a weapon or enemy is placed, its ladder is searched for the current entry that is under the points, then the code walks forward through later rungs of the same family and picks the first rung whose threshold is at or above the points, or the last rung if none is. Weapons keep their bonus class (none, blue or yellow) matching. Scaling is skipped in one map area and in the expansion field when scaling is disabled.

constants.name: no-scaling map area id
constants.unit: ecosystem area id where scaling is not allowed

constants.name: default points sentinel
constants.unit: points; at or above zero the default replaces the kill sum

cards.name: Map area lookup grid
cards.summary: The world is a rectangle 10000 wide and 8000 deep, centered on the origin. A position is shifted, clamped and looked up in a row-compressed table to find its area id.
cards.behavior: X is clamped from minus 5000 to 4999 and Z from minus 4000 to 4000. Both are shifted to be positive and rounded to the nearest integer. Z is divided by the table divisor to choose a row, and when the divisor is 10, X is divided by 10 as well. Each row is a list of run-length segments of area values. The lookup adds segment lengths until it passes X and returns that segment value, or minus 1 if the row is empty or the position is off the end. Area ids then map to climate names, ambient sound names, item sets and terrain traits. Climate, weather and wind all depend on this lookup.

constants.name: coarse divisor
constants.unit: divisor value that triggers x scaling

cards.name: Weapon bonus flags and durability bonus
cards.summary: Weapons carry a bonus flag and a value. The durability bonus is value times 100. A random bonus is picked from the allowed set by shrinking-odds replacement.
cards.behavior: A weapon stores a bit set of bonus types (attack, durability, critical, guard, throw, spread fire, rapid fire, surf master, and a yellow tier marker) and one value. The durability bonus returned by the info object is the value times 100. The pouch code adds the raw value in one path and multiplies a passed value by 100 in another; the source does not explain how the two relate. To pick a random bonus, the picker starts with a count of one, and each allowed bonus type replaces the current choice when a random number below the running count is zero. The count rises only after a replacement, so later types win less often. Fixed values: spread fire is set to 5, and surf master uses a global friction ratio.

constants.name: durability bonus multiplier
constants.unit: durability points per stored value unit

constants.name: random pick start count
constants.unit: initial count for the replacement roll

cards.name: Inventory capacity limits
cards.summary: The pouch holds 420 slots split by category, with stacks of 999 and 50 tabs of 20, and the player can grab 5 objects.
cards.behavior: Capacity is a sum of fixed category sizes: 20 swords, 14 bows, 6 arrow types, 20 shields, 100 armor pieces, 160 materials, 60 foods and 40 key items, which totals 420. A static check enforces this total. A stack holds at most 999. Menu pages hold 20 items and there are at most 50 tabs.

cards.name: Contact impulse filter and scaling
cards.summary: A dynamic body reports a collision impulse only above 5 (or when its flag forces it). The reported value is impulse times mass times a per-body scale, boosted up to double for small light bodies.
cards.behavior: For each colliding pair, an impulse counts only if the body is dynamic and either the raw impulse is above 5 or a special motion flag is set. The value is the raw impulse times body mass times a per-body collision impulse scale. Dynamic bodies with small volume get a factor between 1 and 2: volume 1 or more gives 1, volume 0.2 or less gives 2, and the factor is linear in between. An impulse is then handed to the request system when a motion flag on the other body is set, or when it exceeds the first body maximum impulse (only if that maximum is not negative). If a certain flag is off on the first body, the two impulses are summed first. Small dynamic bodies therefore get up to double the impulse per unit mass.

constants.name: impulse threshold
constants.unit: raw impulse units, physics step rate unverified

constants.name: volume factor low end
constants.unit: volume at which the factor is at its maximum

constants.name: volume factor high end
constants.unit: volume at which the factor is 1

cards.name: Inertia-based motion type and impulse-preserving fixed bodies
cards.summary: A body gets sphere motion when its smallest principal inertia is above 0.8 of its largest, otherwise box motion. Fixed bodies that keep impulses use damping 1 and zero gravity.
cards.behavior: When the inertia changes, the code compares the smallest and largest components. If the smallest is more than 0.8 times the largest, the body is treated as round and uses a sphere inertia model, and otherwise it uses a box model. If the model must change, the motion is recreated and the state is copied over. Character controller bodies skip this. A body flagged as fixed but impulse-preserving gets linear and angular damping of 1 and a gravity factor of 0, so it presumably stays put while still reporting impulses. The sphere rule likely affects how round objects roll.

constants.name: sphere inertia ratio
constants.unit: ratio of smallest to largest inertia component

cards.name: Chemical world rules schema
cards.summary: A world table holds heat, fire, ice, wind and lightning rules: heat transfer speed, ice melt ratios, fire reach, ignition time and lightning range. The tables hold 128 materials, 128 elements and 8 worlds.
cards.behavior: The world entry sets global rates for the elemental simulation: evaporation, heat transfer for everything and for flames, electric conduction speed, burn speed, how far fire reaches an object, a safe distance for the player near fire, discharge range scales, minimum ice size, ice melt ratios against air temperature, warm air, fire and flame, a lift-to-drag ratio for wind, the range of lightning strikes, and the count of frames before characters and objects ignite. The constructor defaults include a heat transfer rate of 24, 90 frames to ignite a character or object and a lightning range of 25 meters per the schema label; the live config is loaded from a resource that is not in this repository. The system has room for 128 materials, 128 elements and 8 worlds.

cards.name: Material and element fields
cards.summary: Each material has heat capacity, thermal conductivity, electrical values, fire proof level 0 to 5 and an ignition point; each element has a lifetime up to 300 frames, temperature, wetness, wind and charge.
cards.behavior: A material is described by physical-style fields: specific heat in joules per gram kelvin, thermal conductivity in watts per meter kelvin, electrical resistivity, capacitance, electromotive force, fire proof level, ignition point, burn speed, wetting amount per area, how much wind force remains, and the names of the elements it produces when it burns, warms, explodes, charges, freezes or gets wet. An element is a short-lived effect such as a flame or a gust with a lifetime in frames, a temperature, a wetting rate, a wind speed, a charge, a shock wave speed, a fire level and a moisture value. The constructor defaults are an ignition point of 100, a burn speed of 1 and an element fire level of 2; the loaded config overrides them.

constants.name: element lifetime limit
constants.unit: frames per the schema label, rate unverified

constants.name: element fire level default
constants.unit: level, constructor default, replaced by config

cards.name: Damage rate and reaction tables
cards.summary: Each actor has 10 damage-source rate multipliers and 40 reaction entries keyed by source and size, giving normal damage, medium damage or blow-off.
cards.behavior: The damage rate table maps a damage source name to a multiplier, with 10 slots that default to 1. A lookup that finds no match returns 0. The reaction table is keyed by the source name joined with a size class, has 40 slots, and returns which reaction the actor plays: normal damage, medium damage or being blown off. Per-actor flags add a critical-hit blow-off, an impulse damage path with a threshold and value per size level (disabled at minus 1 by default), a heavy-break flag, a special-damage ratio and a special-damage add, and a weak point area, with schema defaults of a 4x damage ratio on the first zone and 1x on the second.

cards.name: Status effect settings per actor
cards.summary: Each actor can opt into burn, freeze, shock, wet, drown, cold water, hot water, poison bog, lava and curse effects with damage, time and interval settings.
cards.behavior: The schema has a block per hazard. Fire has five damage levels where minus 1 repeats the previous level, a burn time, and a contact interval. Ice has damage, a freeze time in frames, a flag that attacks shatter it, and a 4x shatter damage ratio. Shock has damage and a time in frames, and lightning has a huge damage value. Water zones have depth thresholds with shallow and deep damage intervals. Hot spring zones heal on intervals. Lava does a huge damage value. The curse effect has a hit value, an interval and a continuing value. The schema defaults are, for example, burn damage 10, ice shatter ratio 4, freeze and shock time 10 frames, lightning and lava damage 999999 and curse damage 30 every 60 units; real values per actor come from resource files that are not in this repository.

cards.name: Player move set catalogue
cards.summary: The decompiled action list shows the player state set: walk, squat, dash, jump, twice jump, wall jump, wall slip, ladder, tree climb, free climb, swim, dive, glide, shield surf, slide, roll, side step, grab and throw, horse and wakeboard.
cards.behavior: Player behavior is a tree of action classes under a few AI roots such as normal, attack, climb, ladder, swim, water fall, grab, sit, camera, beetle, horse and caught. Named actions cover locomotion (move, dash, squat move, step move, side step, front roll, back jump), air control (jump, twice jump, wall jump, wall dash up, wall slip, fall, stop in air, super jump and its charge, glide), water (swim move, swim dash, dive move, water fall jump, wakeboard), climbing (climb rest, ladder start, end and jump, tree climb, hang wall catch, switch hang), combat (cut normal, cut dash, cut jump, spin, guard just, guard slip, guard break, weapon throw, bow, special attack) and states (damage tiers, ice, electric, drown, dead, sleep, sit). Most are thin shells in this decompilation, with a constructor, enter and leave, and sometimes a parameter list, so the list shows the intended move set, not numbers.
capabilities: jump, climb, glide and swim state list

cards.name: Climbing and stamina tunables
cards.summary: The climb action exposes a long list of tunables: stamina drain per direction and slope, charged jump levels, rain slip, flick input thresholds and ray cast lengths. Only the names are decompiled.
cards.behavior: The parameter list shows what the designers tuned. Stamina cost has a constant drain, a drain per jump trigger with three levels, a waiting drain, rates for moving up, sideways and down, and a slope curve with a center, a minimum and a maximum. Rain scales the drain and adds random slips with a base count, a random count, base speed, random speed and a stamina cost per slip. Charged jump has two frame thresholds and a scale range, and a smaller jump is used when stamina is low. Wall probing uses a ray cast offset and length, an end ground angle, a limit wall angle and body fixing offsets. Input has flick thresholds and timings. Noise values for movement and jumping are also listed, presumably as inputs to enemy hearing. The values are not in this repository. Copy the parameter shape, then choose your own numbers.

cards.name: Glider tunables
cards.summary: The glide action exposes a speed cap for two glider levels, body shape offsets, a turn rate range, a wind scale, an over-speed decay and a no-side angle. Only names are decompiled.
cards.behavior: The parameter list shows how gliding is built. There is a maximum glide speed and a second maximum for a level-two glider. Body extents (front, back, side) define the collision shape in the air. Rotation has a maximum, a minimum, a rate and a speed. A wind scale lets the world wind push the glider. An over-speed decay slows the player back to the cap. A no-side angle sets how far the glider can lean before side motion is ignored. The jump-attack action also has a time during which the glider is blocked after a hit. Values are not in this repository.

cards.name: Knockback and launch tunables
cards.summary: Hit reactions use a base speed, an added speed, a maximum and a deceleration per weapon class, plus launch height and impulse presets per source such as wind, toss, horse and shake-off.
cards.behavior: Both the medium and large damage actions read the same four numbers for four weapon classes (one-handed, two-handed, spear, other): base speed, speed added per hit strength, maximum speed and deceleration. The large damage action adds a jump height per class, a block on ragdoll for a short time, linear and roll impulses, and presets for wind blast, being tossed, riding a horse, large creature hits, shake-off and leftover wind. This is a data-driven way to make knockback depend on both the weapon and the cause. Values are not in this repository.

cards.name: Jump attack tunables
cards.summary: The jump attack action has a damage ratio per weapon class, jump speed and height with a short variant, an aim offset, a swing timing before landing, a ground slam height and radius range, and a rumble range.
cards.behavior: The parameter list shows an attack that mixes aerial movement and a landing strike. Damage ratios exist for one-handed, two-handed and spear weapons. The jump has a forward speed and a height, with a short version and a two-handed variant. An aim distance offset and a swing frame count before the ground decide when the strike begins. The falling strike has a trigger height, a radius range that grows with fall, an extra radius for large weapons, a check distance under the player and a large strike radius. Controller rumble has a type and a power range. A timer blocks the glider after the move. Values are not in this repository.

cards.name: Player noise, slip and forbid tunables
cards.summary: The main player AI exposes noise values for equipping, attacking and drawing a bow, a forced slip speed, climb and action forbid timers, a sword search angle, a horse call time and a drown-to-ragdoll water time.
cards.behavior: Noise values tell enemies how loud the player is, one each for equipping, attacking and readying an arrow. A forced slip speed pushes the player down steep ground. Forbid timers stop the player from re-entering an action or climb too soon after leaving it. A wall slip speed, a dash-up speed and an energy charge pair (amount per charge level and start amount) are listed; the exact use of the energy pair is not shown. A sword search angle is listed too. A time in water decides when the player becomes a ragdoll. Values are not in this repository.

cards.name: Horse riding and stress tunables
cards.summary: The riding action models gears, a charge boost with recovery and penalty frames, soothing checks, a familiarity level and a stress meter raised by enemies, damage and impossible input.
cards.behavior: The parameter list describes a mount with moods. Acceleration is capped and drift is tied to turn. After reaching top gear the horse tires for a number of frames. A set of check windows decides whether the rider soothed the horse after the first run, after a run, after top gear, after a jump and after resistance. Familiarity thresholds decide when the horse follows a rail, resists or waits angrily. Resistance picks a gear drop or a steering change by probability, with minimum and maximum frames and an input range. Stress rises from enemies, damage and impossible acceleration, and falls when soothed. Fall checks use a ray cast length and fall heights. Values are not in this repository.

cards.name: Motorcycle, swim mount and surfing tunables
cards.summary: The motorcycle exposes crash speed and speed-drop thresholds, a charge speed, grass and low-tree cutting, four fear speed thresholds and a wheelie range. Horse swimming and water surfing add land search and float depth settings.
cards.behavior: The motorcycle action has a crash velocity and a crash speed change threshold, a fall threshold for throwing the rider off, a charge velocity for attacks, a ride-on delay, drift cut range and intensity on grass, a speed and size for cutting low trees, four speed levels at which animals become scared with a radius and a look-ahead time, a range of angles where spin turns are blocked and where manual wheelies are allowed. Horse swimming searches for land by radius, surface angle, area and interval, and resolves penetration. Water surfing has a rotation speed, wall hit time, fin size, float depth, float cycle time, depth change speed and rail distances. Values are not in this repository.

cards.name: Camera mode catalogue
cards.summary: The camera is a set of action classes: chase, aiming, lock-on, wall, climb object, horse, motorcycle, shield surf, wakeboard, waterfall climb, revolve, tail, finder, and about thirty event cameras. Only a settings picker names its modes.
cards.behavior: Each camera behavior is its own action class under a camera AI tree with roots for game, event, talk, bow and editing. Gameplay modes include chase, aiming (two variants), lock-on, lock-on aiming, climb object, horse (with a lock-on variant for empty target), motorcycle (same), shield surfing, wakeboard, waterfall climb, magnet catch, finder, keep, revolve and tail. Event modes cover scripted moves, polar coordinate moves, look-at, talk with manual control, turns, near and far overrides and save point views. The edit picker has entries for normal, lock-on, wall, subject, bow, crouched bow and bow lock-on. All are empty shells here, so no distance, field of view or damping numbers are available.

cards.name: Interaction target classification
cards.summary: Targets are classed into nine attention types (action, lock, sword search, attack, appeal, jump ride, name balloon, look only, invalid) and a list of about forty action codes with eight priority tiers.
cards.behavior: The enumeration gives the vocabulary of the prompt and lock-on system. Types separate things the player can interact with, lock on to, search a sword toward, attack, appeal to, jump onto to ride, label with a name or just look at. The action code list names the contextual actions: talk, open, pick, catch, skin, sit, pushpull, read, buy, ride, cook, pray, pull out, put and more. A priority enumeration orders candidates: default, enemy, NPC, object at several levels and bullet. Only the enumerations are decompiled; the scoring code is not.
